annotations.description: In a grindy control mirror with the opponent at 14 life, Gem3F Valley passed their entire turn without activating Restless Reef to attack as a 4/4 deathtouch creature. With 10 mana available, they could have animated Reef (4 mana) and still held up counterspell mana (Spell Snare or Essence Scatter). Chip damage with creature-lands is a primary win condition in this type of matchup.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn without taking any action, wasting an opportunity to pressure the opponent.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Reef for {2}{U}{B} to make it a 4/4 deathtouch, attack the opponent (milling them 4 and dealing 4 damage), while holding up remaining mana for countermagic like Spell Snare or Essence Scatter.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Restless Anchorages before declaring attackers against an empty board. With no opposing creatures, two Restless Anchorages could attack as 2/3 flyers for 4 damage and generate Map tokens, applying meaningful pressure at 16 life. The player has abundant mana to activate both while still holding up countermagic.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating any Restless Anchorages, missing an attack opportunity.
annotations.betterLine: Activate both Restless Anchorages ({1}{W}{U} each) to create two 2/3 flyers, then declare them as attackers for 4 damage and 2 Map tokens against the empty board.

annotations.description: During the combat step (before attackers), Gem3F Valley declined to activate Restless Reef to attack as a 4/4 deathtouch creature. With 10 untapped lands and the opponent at 14 life, they could activate Restless Reef for 2UB, attack for 4 damage (milling the opponent 4 cards as well), and still have 6 mana available to hold up countermagic like Three Steps Ahead or Spell Snare. The opponent has no creatures on board to block. In a control mirror where the game is stalling out, dealing 4 damage with a creature land is important for actually closing the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat without activating Restless Reef or attacking.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Reef (2UB) to make it a 4/4 deathtouch, attack for 4 damage and mill 4, while still holding up countermagic with remaining mana.

annotations.description: In a control mirror with 11 lands and nothing else to do, Gem3F Valley passed without using any mana sink abilities. Fountainport could create a Treasure token for {4},{T}, and Demolition Field could destroy one of the opponent's key nonbasic lands (like Restless Anchorage, which is the opponent's primary win condition as a creature-land).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities, wasting all available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Demolition Field targeting one of the opponent's Restless Anchorages (the primary win condition in this board state), or at minimum activate Fountainport to create a Treasure token to accumulate resources.

annotations.description: In a control mirror at turn 23, casting a flash creature (Wan Shi Tong) during their own postcombat main phase taps them out completely, leaving no mana to protect it or interact on the opponent's turn. The opponent has plenty of mana and potential answers. While the ETB card draw provides value regardless, Wan Shi Tong has flash and could be cast at the end of the opponent's next turn instead, allowing Valley to untap and have countermagic mana available to protect it.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Wan Shi Tong, Librarian during their own postcombat main phase, tapping out completely.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn with countermagic mana up (Three Steps Ahead, Spell Snare, Essence Scatter), then cast Wan Shi Tong at the end of opponent's turn using flash, so they untap with mana to protect it with their multiple counterspells.

annotations.description: Wan Shi Tong, Librarian is on the stack (cast for a large X, resulting in the opponent drawing 7 cards and getting a massive flying vigilance creature). Gem3F Valley has Essence Scatter in hand and plenty of untapped mana to cast it, but appears to not counter this game-defining threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Tapped Gloomlake Verge for U without using Essence Scatter to counter Wan Shi Tong, allowing it to resolve and draw 7 cards
annotations.betterLine: Cast Essence Scatter to counter Wan Shi Tong, Librarian, preventing the opponent from getting a huge flying creature and drawing 7 cards

annotations.description: Wan Shi Tong, Librarian is on the stack and Gem3F Valley has Essence Scatter in hand with mana available to cast it. Wan Shi Tong is a massive threat - it's a flyer with vigilance that draws cards and grows whenever the opponent searches their library (which Gem3F Valley's Demolition Fields would trigger). In a control mirror where both players have been grinding for many turns with empty boards, letting a large creature resolve when you have a counter in hand is a critical error. The game note says 'Gem3F Valley draws seven cards' after this, suggesting Wan Shi Tong was cast for X=14 or similar huge value, making it an enormous flying threat that also drew many cards on entry.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Wan Shi Tong, Librarian despite having Essence Scatter and Three Steps Ahead available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Essence Scatter targeting Wan Shi Tong, Librarian to counter this major threat. Alternatively, cast Three Steps Ahead in counter mode to counter it.

annotations.description: Gem25P Drama's opponent just cast Wan Shi Tong, Librarian (on the stack), and Drama has Three Steps Ahead and No More Lies in hand with mana available to counter it. Wan Shi Tong is a significant threat that draws cards and grows whenever the opponent searches their library (Drama has multiple Demolition Fields that trigger searches). Instead of countering this must-answer threat, Drama passed priority, allowing it to resolve. Additionally, Drama has Day of Judgment, Elspeth, and other sorcery-speed plays available but is passing in postcombat main.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority while opponent's Wan Shi Tong, Librarian was on the stack, allowing it to resolve uncountered.
annotations.betterLine: Counter Wan Shi Tong with Three Steps Ahead (counter mode for {1}{U}{U}) or No More Lies ({W}{U}) to prevent the opponent from establishing a card-drawing threat that also punishes Drama's Demolition Field activations.

annotations.description: Gem3F Valley has 2 untapped lands (Undercity Sewers and Island) and 3 copies of Three Steps Ahead in hand, each castable for {U} with the draw-two mode costing +{2} (total {3}{U}). With only 2 mana available, they can't use the draw mode. However, they have an unplayed land in hand (Island, Gloomlake Verge, or Restless Reef) that they should play before passing. They're holding 10 cards and will need to discard down to 7 at end of turn anyway. Playing a land drop costs nothing and increases future mana availability. Additionally, with Wan Shi Tong on board as a threat, having more mana untapped on the opponent's turn is valuable for protecting it with countermagic.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase without playing a land, despite having Island, Gloomlake Verge, and Restless Reef in hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Restless Reef (or another land) from hand before passing. This provides additional mana on future turns and a creature-land threat, and reduces the number of cards that must be discarded to hand size.

annotations.description: Discarded Restless Reef (a creature-land that serves as an additional win condition) instead of a basic land like Island or Gloomlake Verge. With 13 lands already in play, the mana from any additional land is marginal, but Restless Reef's ability to become a 4/4 deathtouch creature provides significant strategic value as a backup threat that dodges board wipes.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Restless Reef as the 3rd discard
annotations.betterLine: Discard Island or Gloomlake Verge instead, keeping Restless Reef as a backup win condition alongside Wan Shi Tong

annotations.description: Gem25P Drama passed priority at end of turn without using mana sinks. They have Fountainport available (untapped, based on having two Fountainports on the battlefield) which could create a Fish token or Treasure token at instant speed on the opponent's end step. They also have Consult the Star Charts and Three Steps Ahead available as instant-speed card draw/selection that could be cast at end of opponent's turn. With 16 lands on the battlefield and the opponent tapped out, this was a prime opportunity to use mana productively.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating any abilities or casting any instant-speed spells.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum, activate Fountainport to create a Fish token (or Treasure token) since the mana would otherwise go to waste. Could also cast Consult the Star Charts with 16 lands to dig deep for answers, or cast Three Steps Ahead in draw mode to find more resources.

annotations.description: Gem25P Drama passed priority during their own combat step without activating Restless Anchorage to attack. They have 16 lands on the battlefield, multiple untapped, and could have animated one or both Restless Anchorages (cost {1}{W}{U} each) to attack as 2/3 flyers. The opponent's Wan Shi Tong is a ground/air blocker with vigilance, but the Anchorages create Map tokens when attacking, providing incremental value. More importantly, the opponent has only 2 untapped lands (Undercity Sewers and Island), limiting their ability to interact. Passing without even attempting to pressure the opponent or generate Map tokens wastes a combat step in what appears to be a long, grindy game where incremental advantages matter.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority during combat without activating any creature-lands or using any abilities.
annotations.betterLine: Activate at least one Restless Anchorage ({1}{W}{U}) to attack as a 2/3 flyer, generating a Map token on attack. The opponent's Wan Shi Tong has flying and vigilance but only has base stats (likely small given it was just cast). Even if blocked, the Map token provides value, and chip damage matters at 16 vs 14 life.

annotations.description: Gem25P Drama passed the turn in postcombat main with Day of Judgment in hand and enough mana to cast it, while the opponent has a Wan Shi Tong, Librarian on the battlefield. Wan Shi Tong is a significant threat that draws cards and grows whenever the opponent searches their library (e.g., from Demolition Field activations). The opponent has multiple Demolition Fields. Leaving Wan Shi Tong alive lets it accumulate value. Day of Judgment costs {2}{W}{W} and Drama has access to Hallowed Fountain x3, Plains, Sunken Citadel (which can produce white), and Island - more than enough untapped mana to cast it. Additionally, Drama could have cast Consult the Star Charts or activated other abilities. Passing here wastes the opportunity to remove the only creature on the board.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in postcombat main phase, ending the turn with no further action.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Day of Judgment to destroy Wan Shi Tong, Librarian, removing the opponent's only threat and preventing it from growing further.

annotations.description: Wan Shi Tong has flying and vigilance, making attacks essentially free against an opponent with no untapped flying blockers (opponent would need to spend mana activating Restless Anchorage). Not attacking wastes free damage in a control mirror where every point matters. The opponent is at 14 life and every attack chips away at their total.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed combat without attacking with Wan Shi Tong, Librarian (flying, vigilance creature) into an empty board.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Wan Shi Tong, Librarian. With vigilance it stays untapped for blocking, and with flying the opponent would need to activate Restless Anchorage (costing them mana) or take damage. Could also activate Restless Reef as an additional attacker to pressure the opponent's life total.

annotations.description: Discarded Spell Snare over Deadly Cover-Up. Spell Snare provides efficient 1-mana countermagic against key opponent spells like Get Lost or No More Lies, while Deadly Cover-Up is actively counterproductive since Valley has the only creature (Wan Shi Tong) and the opponent has none. Deadly Cover-Up would destroy Valley's own win condition if cast.
annotations.actionTaken: Discarded Spell Snare
annotations.betterLine: Discard Deadly Cover-Up, which is the most dead card in hand - it would destroy Valley's own Wan Shi Tong while the opponent has no creatures. Spell Snare's 1-mana efficiency could matter when trying to protect Wan Shi Tong while leaving up other countermagic.
